title: Affine local model at a closed point of a curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve] (integral, separated, of finite type, and of dimension one), and let $x\in X$ be closed [def-weil-closed-points]. There exists an affine open neighbourhood of $x$. For every affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$, put $S=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$, with its $k$-algebra structure induced by $f$, and let $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}S\to X$ be the canonical open immersion onto $U$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $S$ is a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The unique prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ with $\iota_U(\mathfrak q)=x$ is maximal. The germ homomorphism induces an isomorphism of local $k$-algebras
$$S_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{X,x},\qquad r/s\longmapsto r_xs_x^{-1},$$
where localization is as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $r_x$ denotes the germ of the section $r$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. This isomorphism induces an isomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\kappa(x)$ of field extensions of $k$ [def-weil-residue-field], using the structural scalar maps on both sides. Both $S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ are Noetherian local domains of Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. No normality, smoothness or separability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve, opening sentence of proof, expanded by Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (2),(3); affine chart and Noetherianity details recorded in the repair report.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] with $W=X$ to obtain an affine neighbourhood of $x$. Now fix any such $U$ and put $S=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Since $x\in U$, this open is nonempty. The definition of an integral scheme in [def-pc-integral-scheme] makes $S$ an integral domain. The canonical map $\iota_U$ and its point correspondence are given by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. Finite type in [def-pc-curve] implies locally finite type, by the definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to $U$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its ring map is precisely the structural $k\to S$, so $S$ is a finite type $k$-algebra.

The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, each generated by one element. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], applied to the finite type map $k\to S$ just obtained, proves that $S$ is Noetherian.

By [def-weil-open-immersion], $\iota_U$ is a homeomorphism from $\operatorname{Spec}S$ onto $U$, hence the prime $\mathfrak q$ over $x$ is unique and $\{\mathfrak q\}$ is closed: it is the inverse image of the closed set $\{x\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], its closure is $V(\mathfrak q)$, so the only prime containing $\mathfrak q$ is $\mathfrak q$ itself. A maximal ideal containing this proper ideal is prime and therefore equals $\mathfrak q$; hence $\mathfrak q$ is maximal.

source.place: Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible, (1); closed singleton in an affine spectrum

proof.text: Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] gives the isomorphism $\alpha:S_{\mathfrak q}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $\alpha(r/s)=r_xs_x^{-1}$. It sends each $c\in k$ to the germ of its structural section in $S$. Indeed the structural stalk map is obtained by taking germs of the sheaf map defining $f$, as in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] and [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Thus both composites $k\to S_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $k\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ send $c$ to this same germ. The ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is local by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; the target stalk is local by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. A ring isomorphism preserves and reflects units, so it identifies the unique maximal ideals. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of local $k$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, (1),(6); Tag 01HF, example-open-subspace, germ identifications

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak m_x$ for the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. By the preceding maximal-ideal identification, $\alpha$ induces $[a]\mapsto[\alpha(a)]$ from $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ to $\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$, with inverse $[b]\mapsto[\alpha^{-1}(b)]$. These are well defined because $\alpha(\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak m_x$. They are the residue fields $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and $\kappa(x)$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and [def-weil-residue-field]. For $c\in k$ both scalar maps give the class of the germ of $c$, by the preceding step, so this is an isomorphism over $k$.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, (6), followed by quotienting the local rings by their maximal ideals

proof.text: Here is the elementary localization argument for the remaining ring properties. If $J\subset S_{\mathfrak q}$ is an ideal, put $I=\{r\in S:r/1\in J\}$. For $r/s\in J$ one has $r/1=(s/1)(r/s)\in J$; conversely $r\in I$ gives $r/s\in J$. Thus $J=IS_{\mathfrak q}$. Since $S$ is Noetherian, choose finite generators $a_1,\ldots,a_t$ of $I$; their images generate $J$. This proves Noetherianity using [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Since $S$ is a domain and all denominators lie outside the prime $\mathfrak q$, they are nonzero. The fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] therefore says that a zero fraction has zero numerator. A zero product of fractions has numerator $rr^{\prime}=0$, whence one factor is zero; also $1/1\ne0$. Hence $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a domain and, as already noted, local. The isomorphism $\alpha$ carries these properties to $\mathcal O_{X,x}$: ideals and finite generating sets correspond under $\alpha$, as do zero products and units.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, proof of the localization sentence; elementary fraction calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] to $X$: integrality implies irreducibility by [def-pc-integral-scheme], its structure map is locally of finite type by the curve hypothesis, and $U$ is nonempty. The curve hypothesis says that $\sup_{y\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,y}=1$ [def-pc-dimension], and [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] identifies this supremum with the topological Krull dimension of $X$ used in [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic]. Thus $\dim U=\dim X=1$. The homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}S\cong U$ of [def-weil-open-immersion], together with [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring], gives $\dim S=1$. The last sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] now applies to the finite type $k$-algebra domain $S$ and the maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$, and gives $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=\dim S=1$. Finally a ring isomorphism takes prime ideals bijectively to prime ideals by image and inverse image, preserving strict inclusions. Hence $\alpha$ preserves the lengths of prime chains, so $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=1$ as well.
